prompt: A plan assumes infrastructure-less means planning-free. What is the strongest correction?
options: Self-configuration can replace the traffic-demand review
Default settings can supply the service priorities
Demand and link constraints still apply
Network membership can replace the link assessment
explanation: MANET autonomy does not remove capacity, interference or service-planning requirements.

prompt: A demonstration survives one failed path. What conclusion is warranted?
options: It demonstrates resilience under the tested conditions
It guarantees identical performance at every network size
It establishes that physical damage no longer matters
It proves no combination of failures can disrupt communication
explanation: A successful resilience test is evidence for its conditions, not an unlimited guarantee.

prompt: All applications are marked highest priority on a constrained link. What weakness remains?
options: Priority markings physically eliminate interference
The policy no longer distinguishes competing needs
Every application now has unlimited available bandwidth
Membership changes can no longer affect performance
explanation: QoS needs meaningful prioritization; assigning everything the same top priority does not resolve contention.

prompt: Broadcast delivery is proposed for every service regardless of audience. Which concern is most defensible?
options: Unnecessary distribution can consume limited resources
Audience scope has no relationship to network load
Broadcast always provides stronger content encryption
Unicast can never operate in a MANET
explanation: Traffic scope should suit service needs; all-informed distribution is not automatically efficient for every use.

prompt: An integration test confirms voice compatibility but documents no security properties. What cannot be inferred?
options: That the exchanged voice meets required protection
That the tested configuration supported that voice service
That security documentation still needs review
That a voice exchange occurred in the test
explanation: The source distinguishes encrypted and clear waveforms; successful exchange alone proves no required protection level.

prompt: Management messages are authenticated but confidentiality has not been assessed. Which conclusion is sound?
options: Confidentiality and authentication mean the same thing
Authentication alone does not establish secrecy
Radio frequency hopping settles management-data confidentiality
An authenticated message is necessarily unreadable to others
explanation: Authentication and confidentiality are different properties even when a protocol supports both.

prompt: A product supports several services, but a chosen configuration has not been tested with the required mix. What is missing?
options: Proof that a capability list replaces acceptance testing
Evidence for the configured end-to-end service requirements
A reason to assume every configuration has identical capacity
A requirement to discard every supported service
explanation: Advertised or listed capability does not establish performance for a particular configuration and workload.

prompt: Frequency hopping is cited as proof that interference cannot affect service. Which response is accurate?
options: Security features eliminate all need for link measurements
Resistance does not guarantee immunity
Any hopping system guarantees error-free communication
Interference can affect only wired systems
explanation: The source's resistance claims should not be inflated into immunity or universal service guarantees.

prompt: A built-in test passes but an external cable is visibly damaged. Which conclusion is best?
options: The damage can be ignored unless a user complains
A passing BIT proves every external component is undamaged
The physical defect still requires authorized attention
Software version information repairs the cable automatically
explanation: Test scope matters; a passing result does not override observed damage outside or beyond what it establishes.

prompt: Replacing a part improves symptoms without identifying the original cause. What should the report distinguish?
options: Observed improvement from a confirmed diagnosis
Repair completion from all future performance guarantees
A guess from evidence by calling both verified
Equipment age from its network address format
explanation: A repair may improve behavior without proving causation; accurate records should preserve that distinction.

prompt: Maintenance is rushed and verification omitted to save time. What risk does the model identify?
options: An unresolved fault may return to service undetected
A signed repair form guarantees functional correctness
Identification becomes unnecessary if a part was changed
Cleaning automatically proves every network function works
explanation: The final verification step is necessary to establish that relevant faults have actually been corrected.

prompt: The radio operates alone but fails in its vehicle installation. What is the sound diagnostic scope?
options: Ignore the installation because the same radio is present
Declare the handheld permanently defective without comparison
Use only a screenshot of the standalone display
Include adapter, power, connections and relevant test paths
explanation: The adapter and installation add dependencies; the source includes tests covering the vehicular arrangement.

prompt: Two tests report similar RSSI but different delivery results. Which explanation is most defensible?
options: Packet counts must be wrong whenever RSSI matches
Node names determine delivery independently of all links
Equal RSSI guarantees equal delivery under every condition
Strength is not a complete quality measure
explanation: SNR, load and other conditions can differ; no single strength measurement establishes total performance.

prompt: A failed ping and successful application exchange occur together. What should be checked?
options: Whether a failed ping proves every application is offline
Whether application success is impossible by definition
Diagnostic settings and the tested paths
Whether all performance records should be deleted
explanation: Diagnostic responses and application traffic can have different conditions; investigate rather than overgeneralize.

prompt: A test changes packet size, interval and destination simultaneously. Why is the comparison difficult?
options: Every destination must produce the same result
Changing a test parameter guarantees an improved network
The packet counters stop being numerical values
Multiple changed variables obscure the cause of a difference
explanation: Controlled comparisons help attribute effects; simultaneous changes make causal conclusions weaker.

prompt: A student proposes using protected recovery functions during ordinary operation without authorization. Which principle applies?
options: A recovery label means the function has no operational effect
Use only authorized functions for the defined maintenance purpose
Protected functions are unrestricted if the user is curious
Restoring parameters guarantees all services regardless of context
explanation: The lesson separates protected functions and maintenance modes; their purpose does not waive authorization.

prompt: An integrator forwards data successfully but exposes it to unintended service networks. How should the result be judged?
options: Service separation is irrelevant after data arrives
Successful forwarding proves security is fully adequate
More unintended recipients demonstrate better interoperability
Functional exchange passed, but traffic-control requirements failed
explanation: Integration must satisfy both functional and security requirements; one does not substitute for the other.

prompt: Local voice, remote data and management tests each pass separately. What is still worth validating?
options: Whether separate successes guarantee all concurrent workloads
Whether management access replaces application testing
The required services together under representative conditions
Only the spelling of the integrator's product name
explanation: Separate tests establish limited facts; concurrent end-to-end requirements can expose interactions and load constraints.

prompt: A repair is called permanent after a brief idle-network test. Which qualification is needed?
options: Assume idle performance is the maximum possible demand
Claim the short test proves every future workload
Replace the measurements with an unqualified assurance
State test scope and verify representative required loads
explanation: Verification should reflect intended conditions and report its limits, not promise performance beyond its evidence.

prompt: An upgrade adds video while preserving the old traffic policy unchanged. What should a review examine?
options: Only whether the old policy file has the same name
Whether adding a capability removes all prior constraints
Service demand, traffic boundaries and measured performance
Only whether the new camera looks modern
explanation: New service demand can change capacity and security needs; integration planning must reassess both.
